messages:
Maya Patel: Quick copy check — onboarding noticed the inline retry CTA after a 429. Current copy is "Rate limited — try again". Feels a bit abrupt. Thoughts?
Liam Chen: Agree, feels terse. Maybe we can make it actionable: "Rate limited — try again in 10s"?
Sofia Ruiz: I like adding a countdown if we can. But if we can’t show seconds reliably, maybe "Please retry in a few seconds" is safer and more accessible.
Samir Kapoor: From engineering: we can expose the retry-after header when present. Otherwise it's a best-effort estimate.
Maya Patel: Good to know. Accessibility angle — should we avoid words like "please" vs direct? UX usually prefers friendly.
Liam Chen: Friendly + succinct is the goal. Also consider screen readers: short sentences, and add role=alert? That’s infra, but copy should be clear.
Sofia Ruiz: Proposed variants: 1) "Rate limit reached. Try again in 10s." 2) "Too many requests — try again shortly." 3) "We’re a bit busy. Retry in a few seconds." Which reads best?
Maya Patel: I prefer #1 when we have a numeric retry; otherwise #2. #3 feels too casual for enterprise customers.
DesignBot: [screenshot uploaded] mock: retry CTA inline, small helper text under button.
Liam Chen: Small nit: the helper text currently truncates on narrow widths — use shorter phrase ~20 chars. "Try again in 10s" is 16 chars, good.
Samir Kapoor: Edge case: sometimes backend returns >60s. If it's long, we should give an alternative: "Queue for later" or show a link to docs.
Sofia Ruiz: How about suffix with a link: "Try again in 10s — or view rate limits" (link). But inline might be crowded. Maybe a small info icon that opens docs.
Maya Patel: Agree. For the confirmation dialog when clicking retry after many failures, do we need a safety message? Probably not.
Liam Chen: Also consider translations — short phrases translate better. Avoid idioms. "Too many requests" is common HTTP phrasing but not user-friendly. "Rate limit reached" is developer-y. "Try again shortly" is neutral.
Sofia Ruiz: Accessibility: ensure the helper text is visible to high-contrast themes and announced via ARIA when it changes. Write copy that reads naturally in voiceover: e.g., "Rate limit reached. Try again in ten seconds." (spell out numbers for screen readers?)
Samir Kapoor: Engineering prefers numerals for parsing, but we can render full text for announce and numeral visually. So copy could be dual: visually "Try again in 10s" with aria-label="Try again in ten seconds".
Maya Patel: Final proposal: when Retry-After present -> helper text visual: "Try again in 10s"; aria-label: "Try again in ten seconds"; link icon next to it "Why this happened" opens docs. When absent -> "Try again shortly".
Liam Chen: LGTM. Also add microcopy for tooltip on the info icon: "Your request exceeded the rate limit. See docs for limits and best practices." Keep tooltip <= 120 chars.
Sofia Ruiz: Tooltip draft: "Request rate exceeded. Learn how to reduce retries and use caching." (95 chars)
Maya Patel: Nice. Quick accessibility nit: tooltip must be keyboard focusable and readable by screen readers. We should annotate the copy accordingly in the dev ticket.
DesignBot: Created follow-up ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-4923 — contains comps and copy variants.
Samir Kapoor: I’ll pick up implementation: will add aria-labels and expose retry-after to client when available. Plan to ship canary tomorrow.
Maya Patel: Thanks team — I’ll update the design mock and add the final copy to the ticket. :thumbsup:
